editorial.headline: Electrical Road Equipment: Foreign-Open Nationally, Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers electrically based road equipment—street lighting, electronic traffic signs and signals—and is open to foreign investment nationally, with Bali’s moratorium not blocking it at the Large scale.
editorial.body:
Electrical road equipment is the subject of this activity: the installation, maintenance and repair of powered roadside systems that help a road be seen, read and navigated. The stated field encompasses street lighting, electronic traffic signs and traffic-signal equipment, along with the practical work of fitting, servicing and restoring those systems. Its boundary is technological as much as operational: the equipment is electrically based, and the activity follows it across its useful cycle of installation, upkeep and repair.

Registration is open across every recorded scale—Micro, Small, Medium and Large—so the classification speaks to businesses operating at each of those sizes. That breadth does not turn it into a general roadworks label. The work remains precisely about electrical road equipment and the named functions performed on it. The relevant business description is anchored in powered lighting, electronic signage and signalling systems, and in the installation, maintenance or repair work identified by the scope.

At the national level, the foreign-investment status is Open, and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%. The record therefore gives a straightforward national starting point: this activity is foreign-open at that stated ceiling. There is no second national percentage or additional condition supplied in the record to dilute the point. The important distinction is then geographic rather than numerical—whether Bali’s province-wide PMA moratorium alters the result.

In this case, Bali does not reverse the national position. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not blocked for PMA registration by the island-wide, permanent moratorium that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The stated reason concerns the Large scale, where the OSS risk is Medium-High/High; on that basis it is not blocked by the moratorium. That is the clean local reading: foreign openness nationally is intact, while Bali’s recorded moratorium does not bar this activity. No Bali-specific foreign-ownership cap or additional local condition is supplied in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not reverse the national position: the recorded moratorium does not bar this activity.
